winner.title: Tuvalu's finger-licking baked taro dish (talo tokotokoi)
winner.source: The Spinoff (Marama T-Pole with Aunty Fulu; written by Sela Jane Hopgood)

evidence.authenticity: Shared by a Tuvaluan-descent cook and her aunty with cultural context; real Tuvaluan taro + coconut cream dish, but uses pink taro (not pulaka), is sweetened, and has no fish, so it is only the pulaka-and-coconut-cream half of the dish
evidence.precision: 400ml coconut cream, 2 pink taro, 1 cup sugar, 180 degrees, prep 20 min / cook 1h30; cues: taro smell fills kitchen, crack lines, cream has no small bubbles and thickens; no pan sizes, no taro weights
evidence.testing: Family recipe with some reasoning (peeling tip, stirring direction lore); no test kitchen
evidence.photos: Photo captions for baking taro and finished dish; not full process coverage
evidence.efficiency: Cream stirred 30 min while taro bakes; sensible parallel work
evidence.access: Pink taro from Samoa/Fiji available at Pacific/Asian markets; no substitute stated; no fish component

winner.why: It is the only Tuvaluan-sourced recipe with real quantities and cues, but it lacks the fish and uses pink taro, so it does not satisfy the dish.

runnerUp.title: Tuvalu Tuna

evidence.precision: Volume amounts, but 'done to preference', 'large skillet or wok', no authorship

runnerUp.why: Gives the coconut fish half only, with no pulaka and loose precision.

candidates.disqualified: Fijian dish (ika lolo), not Tuvaluan; no amounts for fish, coconut cream or oil
Overview page only; no recipe amounts or steps for pulaka or coconut fish

notes: No tested web recipe exists for pulaka served with coconut fish. Sources describe tulolo (beaten pulaka with coconut cream), fekei, and boiled pulaka with coconut cream alongside fish, but give no measurements. Best path may be to compose the dish: a tested taro recipe (e.g. the Spinoff method, or boiled taro) plus a coconut fish recipe, with taro as the pulaka substitute (fresh pulaka is not sold in the US). Consider retrying with a different dish name such as tulolo or kakakai.
